first-couple-ocean-steady.label: First-time couple, wants the ocean, sensitive stomach

recommendations.hook: Midship balcony where the ocean view meets calm waters
recommendations.reason: 10168 sits in the heart of the ship on deck 10, low enough to keep motion minimal for your partner's queasy stomach while still giving you both that ocean outlook you want. Being midship and several decks down means you're in the sweet spot for stability, and you'll wake to the water without the rocking that side cabins can sometimes catch.

recommendations.hook: Starboard balcony in the quiet center, stable and peaceful
recommendations.reason: This teal balcony is positioned right in the middle section of deck 10, offering the same motion-reduction benefits as 10168. The location keeps you away from busy elevator banks and high-traffic areas, so both of you get the sleep you need. You'll have your ocean view and a genuinely restful night.

recommendations.hook: Ocean-facing perch built for light sleepers and steady seas
recommendations.reason: Also a teal cabin in the calm midship area, 10188 gives you the same stability advantage. It's positioned far enough from service corridors and public spaces that the quiet will hold. Since it's your second cruise, you already know what you want—this delivers the ocean view plus the tranquility without compromise.

recommendations.hook: Higher deck balcony—still stable, with the bonus of a broader horizon
recommendations.reason: Moving up to deck 11 in this mint cabin actually keeps motion low because you're still well-centered on the ship. Being a deck higher opens up the view without putting you in rough water. If your partner doesn't feel queasy at all during your first cruise, this gives you a bit more visual drama without any real downside.

recommendations.hook: Central balcony with unobstructed ocean and peaceful surroundings
recommendations.reason: This teal cabin clusters in the same stable midship zone on deck 10. It's a quiet neighborhood without the hum of nearby crew passages or the thump of deck above. Solid choice if 10168 or 10178 book before you get there—same benefits, same reliable sleep.

recommendations.hook: Teal balcony where higher means calmer, ocean front and centered
recommendations.reason: Deck 11, teal cabin, midship positioning—it checks all three boxes. You're up a level for a fresher view, but still in the ship's most stable zone. Light sleepers and queasy partners both benefit from the centered location and distance from noise sources.

steerClear.reason: This orange cabin is at the far forward end of deck 10, where the bow pitches more noticeably and your partner will feel the motion. Combined with its distance from the center, it's not worth the risk for someone prone to queasiness.

Gray cabin near the stern on deck 10—aft sections tend to have more vibration and movement, especially at sea. For a light sleeper and someone concerned about tummy troubles, this is working against you both.
Salmon cabin on deck 12 far aft; higher decks at the stern amplify motion and noise from the engines. You'd wake up to movement, not ocean peace.

couple-ocean-balcony-treat.label: Couple treating themselves to a great balcony

recommendations.hook: Higher-deck balcony, quieter, better views
recommendations.reason: Deck 15 naturally feels more removed from the ship's main activity. This cabin gives you distance from the crowds and noise you want to avoid, plus you're higher up so the ocean views open out more. It's a nicer setting for two people treating yourselves.

recommendations.hook: Balcony with genuine seclusion from foot traffic
recommendations.reason: 10734 is positioned in a quieter section well away from the central corridors and activity areas. You'll feel less exposed to the constant movement of other guests, which matters when you're looking for a peaceful retreat, not just a room with a view.

recommendations.hook: Upgraded balcony on a quieter upper deck
recommendations.reason: Higher decks tend to be calmer, and this one's positioned away from the main elevator bank and busy areas. The setup gives you the treat-yourself feeling you're after—a nice balcony in a genuinely peaceful corner of the ship.

recommendations.hook: Ocean-facing retreat in the calm midship zone

steerClear.reason: This is near the forward elevator bank on Deck 10, meaning constant foot traffic and noise from people coming and going all day and night. Not the peaceful setting you're looking for.

Deck 9 in this section is near central stairwells and higher-traffic corridors. The balcony won't make up for the noise and constant movement around the cabin.

It's the anniversary upgrade that actually feels like one.

recommendations.hook: Premium suite on the highest deck—the crown of the ship

recommendations.hook: Top suite option with uncluttered balcony and guest privileges

recommendations.hook: Suite with room to spare and all the VIP amenities inside

steerClear.reason: This is a green cabin on Deck 10—a lower deck that's closer to engine noise and more foot traffic from crew corridors. For a no-budget-ceiling anniversary, you're settling for a room that sacrifices the height, view, and peace that a higher-deck suite delivers.

Green category on Deck 11 means you're in a mid-deck position with a smaller, less premium balcony than the top-tier suites. At your budget level, this doesn't give you the 'best room on the ship' feeling you're after—it's comfortable but not the occasion-worthy space an anniversary deserves.

This is a standard blue balcony cabin on a high deck, not a suite. You'll lose the suite perks (concierge, priority dining, cabin service) and the dedicated space that separates a celebration suite from a regular stateroom. Without those extras, you're paying for height alone.

recommendations.hook: Steps from the pool, shows, and occasional conga line

You'll hear life on the ship, but you're not directly above or below the loudest spots.

recommendations.hook: Central location with quick access to family hangouts

recommendations.hook: Deck 10 positioning puts you near the fun without the chaos
recommendations.reason: 10220 lands in a part of Deck 10 that balances access to the main entertainment and dining venues while avoiding the densest corridor zones. recommendations.hook: Action-adjacent cabin for families who want easy reach

You get a cabin that's genuinely useful for active families, not one you have to think twice about leaving.

recommendations.hook: Mid-deck placement serves families who want constant access
recommendations.reason: 10206 sits in a section of Deck 10 that feeds naturally toward the heart of the ship's daytime spaces. For a family comfortable with noise, this is actually a feature—you're where the energy is, and your kids won't be bored or frustrated by a long walk to get anywhere fun.

recommendations.hook: Central Deck 10 location keeps your family in motion

steerClear.reason: This cabin is positioned at the far end of Deck 10, away from the main pool and entertainment zones. For a family that wants to be near all the action, you'd spend half your cruise walking to get anywhere fun.

Located on Deck 10 but isolated from the primary activity areas. You'd sacrifice the proximity to activities your family is looking for in exchange for a cabin that feels disconnected from the ship's heartbeat.

steerClear.reason: This is marked green (likely a suite or premium category), which means it's pricing above standard interior and defeats your lean-budget goal. You'll pay significantly more for features your family doesn't need.
Salmon category on Deck 12 signals a specialty cabin—higher rate for extras you're not shopping for. Stick with the plain white and mint interiors to keep money in your pocket for the trip itself.

recommendations.hook: Midship quiet on a lower deck, away from foot traffic

recommendations.hook: Deep midship berth with ocean view, minimal disturbance

recommendations.hook: Interior cabin in the heart of the ship, pure silence

recommendations.hook: White cabin in the calm zone, steady and still

steerClear.reason: This gray cabin sits far forward on deck 10, near the bow, where you'll feel more motion and pick up engine noise. Not what you signed up for when you booked for peace.
White cabin but positioned toward the aft end of deck 11, close to public corridors and elevator banks where foot traffic builds late into the night. Light sleepers find this spot disruptive.
Deck 12's higher position and green category place it near the ship's atrium and public areas, making it a pass for anyone hunting quiet. You'd trade tranquility for a view of the chaos.

Salmon category on deck 12—these are specialty or restricted-view cabins, often cheaper for a reason. No real ocean access, and you'd be compromising the view you're willing to trade budget flexibility for.

recommendations.hook: Interior cabin, dead center of the ship—lowest cost option
